title: Typed Continuation Domains
purpose: Refine WF(C) by defining explicit domain typing for continuation expressions across meta, affect/effect, projection, continuation, observation, and operational-regime layers.
core_claim: A continuation expression is well-formed only when its endpoints and operators are domain-compatible.

canonical_claims.statement: A continuation expression is well-formed only when its endpoints and operators are domain-compatible.
A_meta retains TYPE_META and must not be rebound implicitly.
A|E retains TYPE_AFFECT_EFFECT and must not be substituted into meta-domain bindings.
Projection outputs and D(*|*) are TYPE_PROJECTION and remain domain-local to the projection layer.
Continuation expressions and NF(C) are TYPE_CONTINUATION and compose only when typed endpoints match.
Cross-domain substitution without explicit projection, binding, or transition rule fails WF(C).

formal_objects.name: Typed Continuation Domains
formal_objects.definition: Explicit domain typing constraints for continuation expressions across meta, affect/effect, projection, continuation, observation, and operational-regime layers.

composition_guard: C(A,B) ∘ C(B,C) is lawful only when codomain/domain matching and type compatibility both hold.
domain_error_rule: If a continuation crosses domains without an explicit projection, binding, or transition rule, WF(C) fails.
validation_requirements: WF(C) now has explicit type guards.
Cross-domain substitution is forbidden without explicit transition.
A_meta/B_meta cannot be confused with affect/effect A/E.
Reduction and composition now require both well-formedness and type compatibility.
